faq.question: How do I free up space on Android without deleting photos?
faq.answer: Back your photos up to Google Photos, then use its Free up space option to remove only the copies on your phone. Then archive apps you rarely use, clear app caches, delete large WhatsApp media and old downloads, and empty your Files app's bin.

faq.question: Is it safe to clear cache on Android?
faq.answer: Yes. The cache holds temporary files that apps rebuild when needed. Clearing it doesn't sign you out or delete your data. Clearing storage or data is different: it resets the app completely.

faq.question: What does archiving an app do?
faq.answer: It removes most of the app's files but keeps your data and the icon on your home screen, with a small cloud on it. Tapping the icon downloads the app again and you carry on where you left off. Google says it frees up to about 60% of the app's space.

faq.question: Why is my storage still full after deleting files?
faq.answer: Your Files or Gallery app probably moved them to a bin, where they still take space for a period, often 30 days. Empty the bin to free the space immediately.

faq.question: Will Google Photos "Free up space" delete my photos?
faq.answer: Only the copies on your phone, and only for items already backed up. They stay in Google Photos and at photos.google.com. Check that backup is complete before you use it, and remember they won't show in your phone's built-in gallery app.
